2. Shahjalal Mojumder, Managing Director of Grand Bashia Company Limited (shortly, Grand Bashia), as petitioner, filed Writ Petition No.8086 of 2012, contending, inter alia, that after the independence of Bangladesh the proprietor of Ferdous Tannery and some other persons left Bangladesh abandoning their properties. Thereafter, the Government in 1972 made a list of abandoned properties and became owner of those properties left by the respective owners including the properties left by the proprietor of Ferdous Tannery. A Gazette Notification dated 13.01.1972 was also published for those abandoned properties. Subsequently, the Government took a decision to auction sale the said enlisted abandoned properties. Accordingly, the Government published auction notice in 1978 including the properties owned by Ferdous Tannery. Writ Petitioner-Grand Bashia participated in the auction bid and being highest bidder purchased the properties of Ferdous Tannery. Accordingly, an agreement for sale was executed between the Government and Grand Bashia on 25.02.1978. Thereafter, Grand Bashia paid the auction money and the Government on 08.09.1978 handed over the ownership and possession of the properties of Ferdous Tannery in favour of Grand Bashia. A sub-kabala deed being registered deed No.45 dated 28.12.1992 was also executed and registered by the Government in favour of Grand Bashia Grand Bashia has been enjoying and possessing the said properties by mutating its name and paying rents to the Government. The writ petitioner-Grand Bashia by the aforesaid registered deed purchased 1.34½  acres of land and structures thereon with machineries including .0948 acres of land of Mouza-Lalbagh, C.S. Khatian No.11102, S.A. Khatian No.991, R.S. Khatian No.4046, C.S. Plot No.3435, S.A. Plot No.2579, R.S. Plot No.4589. 

 3. The Commissioner of Police proposed to take monthly rent of House No.92, Water Works Roads, Pasta, Lalbagh, Dhaka under Mouza-Lalbagh corresponding to S.A. Khatian No.991, S.A. Plot No.2579 corresponding to R.S. Khatian No.4046, R.S. Plot No.4589 measuring an area of .0948 acres of land including building thereon. Accordingly, there was an agreement between Grand Bashia and the Commissioner of Police for monthly tenancy of the House for 1(one) year at a monthly rental of Tk.5,000/-. The Commissioner of Police also paid monthly rent to Grand Bashia according to the monthly rental agreement. Eventually, the agreement was not renewed due to the poor condition of the House situated upon .0948 acres of land. All on a sudden, the City Corporation directed Grand Bashia by letter dated 26.11.1994 to vacate the said property in order to demolish struc-tures of the same. Earlier, respondent No.5, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka issued a notice under section 6 of the Immovable Property Acquisition and Requisition Ordinance, 1982 (hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance) to Grand Bashia on 24.08.2002 in L.A. Case No.8 of 2001-02 to acquire an area of .0948 acres of land of Mouza-Lalbagh, C.S. Khatian No.11102, C.S. Plot No.3435 for construction of a house and Police Fari. Grand Bashia gave reply to the said letter informing that 1.34½ acres of land was purchased by the petitioner on 28.12.1992 from the Government and the same was mortgaged in favour of Janata Bank (shortly, the Bank) for obtaining loan of Tk.36,00,000/-; that a Civil Suit for eviction was pending before the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka being Title Suit No.76 of 2002; that Civil Revision No.121 of 2001 was also pending before the High Court Division arising out of the said suit. The Bank also filed an objection to respondent No.5 by a letter dated 16.06.2002 stating that the proposed property for requisition was mortgaged in favour of the Bank and the Bank would not be able to recover the loan money in case of acquisition. However, the proposed acquisition of property was not completed as the Ministry concerned did not place any fund for acquisition. As a result, the operation of L.A. Case No.8 of 2001-02 was cancelled. Suddenly, the petitioner Grand Bashia came to know that some Government officials in connivance with some local people purposely acquired the property. Upon inquiry from the L.A. Office Grand Bashia managed to obtain a photostat copy of the notice under section 7 of the Ordinance, but the said notice was never served upon the oetitioner. However, the notices were served upon one Md. Shafique, Md. Rafique, Md. Faruque, Md. Gulzar ali are sons of Moula Box, Water Works Road, Lalbagh, Dhaka without mentioning any holding number therein. Therefore, the operation of the aforesaid L.A. Case on the basis of the aforesaid notice is malafide, illegal and not binding upon Grand Bashia. Grand Bashia also served a legal notice to the L.A. Office but without any result. In the circumstances, the petitioner-Grand Bashia filed Writ Petition No.8086 of 2012 and obtained a Rule Nisi. 

 4. Respondent No.5, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka contested the Rule Nisi by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that notices were duly served upon the owners of the properties in L.A. Case No.14/2010-2011 for acquisition of the property by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and assessment notice dated 11.06.2010 under section 7 of the Ordinance was also issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka; that .0948 acres of land of R.S. Plot No.4589 corresponding to S.A. Plot No.2579, C.S. Plot No.3435, under C.S. Khatian No.11102, S.A. Khatian No.991, R.S. Khatian No.4046, P.S. Lalbagh, Dhaka was acquired for the purpose of constructing Lalbagh Police Fari legally; that the sale deed dated 28.12.1992 of Grand Bashia does not contain the acquired property; that fund for compensation has already been placed by the requiring body; that acquisition process being completed, the acquired property vested with the Government and, as such, the writ petition is not maintainable.
